note: Canada, read in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (SOR/2002-227, current to 2026-09-30, last amended 2026-07-15) and the Citizenship Act, section 5, as Justice Laws serves them (read 2026-10-30). A performing artist appearing alone or in a group in a performance not primarily for film, television or radio works without a permit (section 186, the work engine's reading); to live and work in Canada, as an actor in a film or series among others, a foreigner needs a work permit, $155 to process, with an employer's offer of employment (and the employer's compliance fee of $230 where the work is exempt from a labour market impact assessment), read as work for the sponsor; it is applied for abroad, at the border or in Canada. The permit's length is the employment's and no fixed term is stated. Permanent resident status allows any work; its right of permanent residence fee ($500 in the text, indexed every two years from 30 April 2022) and the processing fees are indexed figures the regulation does not print as they stand, and IRCC's fee list (canada.ca) did not answer this client, so no fee is kept. Citizenship asks 1,095 days' physical presence in the five years before applying; each day as a temporary resident before permanent residence counts as half a day, up to 365, so the work permit's years count in part. Decision times are not in the law.

sources.title: Citizenship Act, s. 5 (Justice Laws)
sources.said: been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days during the five years immediately before the date of his or her application ... for every day during which the person was physically present in Canada as a temporary resident or protected person under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act before becoming a permanent resident, the person accumulates half of a day of physical presence, up to a maximum of 365 days
